detail.abstract: The Panel Study of Income Dynamics is a unique resource for studying the influence of early and adult life circumstances on health and mortality in later life (McGonagle et al. 2012). Since the late 1990s, the study has included questions about health status, health conditions, health behaviors, health insurance, and health care expenditures. Retrospective questions about childhood health have been asked since 2007. The objective of this brief report is to provide a comparison over 15 years between the health status and health condition data that have been collected in the PSID with estimates from the most widely used nationally representative health survey, the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). We begin by briefly summarizing the health information that has been collected throughout the history of the PSID. title: Towards a Theory of Modular Natives

detail.title: Towards a Theory of Modular Natives
detail.abstract: First, we present a new theory, the "theory of modular natives." A modular native is a basic building block that was born modular, e.g., a solar or a battery cell. The theory predicts that using modular natives in building things reduces complexity and risk and improves predictability, resulting in better outcomes and faster scale-up. Second, we test the theory on the largest dataset of its kind. We find, at a high level of statistical significance (p < 0.001), that modular natives operate under a fundamentally different risk regime than other project types, with finite and predictable risk, in contrast to non-natives that have infinite and unpredictable risk. The findings help explain why modularity is key to successful building while bespokeness often leads to failure. Third, we relate our findings to economic and geopolitical development, arguing that China understands modular natives and scale-up better than any other geography and that this is key to China's swiftly growing dominance in renewables, batteries, EVs, robots, etc. We argue that China's mastery of modularity and scale-up is a major innovation in its own right, among the greatest and most impactful in human history, falsifying the common notion that China cannot innovate. Business and government outside China ignore these findings at their peril. Finally, we spell out policy and practice implications and identify areas for further research.

title: The Deliberate Amputation of Descartes’ Theory: The Explosion of U.S. Public Debt Is Not a Policy Failure but a First-Physics Illusion That Responsibility Can Be Annihilated

detail.title: The Deliberate Amputation of Descartes’ Theory: The Explosion of U.S. Public Debt Is Not a Policy Failure but a First-Physics Illusion That Responsibility Can Be Annihilated

detail.abstract: Over the past four decades, U.S. public debt has risen roughly twenty-one-fold, while nominal GDP has grown only about sevenfold. This widening "alligator mouth" is not merely a policy failure but a symptom of a deeper conceptual error. For centuries, the dominant scientific paradigm-what I call First Physics-has modelled the world in terms of matter, energy, and information, while treating responsibility and meaning as external to its formal language. Enabled by a selective, post-Cartesian amputation of God from Descartes' original system, this First Physics operating system has encouraged the illusion that responsibility can be diluted, exported, or made to disappear. In response, I propose Second Physics: a relational framework that treats responsibility as a conserved quantity in its own right. The Law of Conservation of Responsibility states that responsibility cannot be destroyed; it can only be transferred across agents, places, and generations. Using long-run data on U.S. federal debt and GDP, I show that the current trajectory embodies a structurally unsustainable configuration: an overextended, debt-financed, desire-driven capitalism-what I describe as a second Tower of Babel-quietly supported by the West as a whole, Japan included. Second Physics does not condemn the American dream, the dollar, capitalism, or growth as such. Rather, it makes mathematically explicit why the particular First Physics operating system under which they have been combined has reached its structural limit.

title: How Public Officials Decide: Experimental Evidence on Deliberation in the Public Sector

detail.title: How Public Officials Decide: Experimental Evidence on Deliberation in the Public Sector
detail.abstract: How can governments encourage public officials to make decisions in the public interest, when officials differ in their motivations? We address this question using an experiment with currently serving middle management public officials in the context of weak institutional capacity. The experiment compares decisions made under personal framing with decisions made under an identical professional (policy) framing, allowing us to test whether officials apply the same care and judgement when deciding on behalf of the public as they do when deciding for themselves. We find that, on average, officials make decisions differently across the two frames, and that this divergence is driven by officials with lower public service motivation. We then introduce a simple, low-cost institutional intervention by randomly assigning officials to make joint decisions with a peer. Relative to officials who repeat the task individually, deliberation shifts decisions in mixed-motivation teams toward the choices of more motivated officials. Together, our results highlight how organizational features such as peer deliberation can complement selection and incentives in shaping public sector decision-making.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the strategic formation of teams within organizations with moral hazard, focusing on the impact of agents' altruism on incentive structures. detail.abstract: This paper investigates the role of institutional failures in the establishment and aggravation of the 1997 economic crisis within the context of the post-1987 democratic transition of South Korea. This paper will propose that the 1997 economic crisis cannot only be explained by short-term macroeconomic failures but also that institutional failures played a significant part in it. Although political pluralism is increased during the time of democratic transition, the informal discipline system that operated during the authoritarian period lacked strength, but it failed to develop proper rule-of-law-based regulatory institutions, creating areas of supervisory weakness in the financial system, along with over-borrowing by the giant business groups and a buildup of systemic risk.

detail.title: Management Controls in Hierarchies

detail.abstract: We study management controls (MCs) in a multi-level hierarchy, where senior managers use MCs to motivate middle managers, who in turn use MCs to motivate rank-and-file employees. We draw on existing control typologies (Merchant and Van der Stede 2017) to develop and validate new measures of the degree to which controls are standardized versus customized. In a field setting, we find that middle managers with larger spans of control prioritize standardized over customized controls. However, employee task diversity weakens the effectiveness of standardized controls and moderates the relation between span of control and control choices. Turning to outcomes of these control choices, we document negative associations between the use of standardized controls and both employee satisfaction and promotion frequency. These findings highlight a tension: standardized controls reduce costs for middle managers but impose costs on subordinate employees. Together, our evidence sheds light on the role of a middle manager’s span of control in MCs implementation and reveals trade-offs associated with increased reliance on standardized controls.

title: Measuring the Impact of Inventory and Marketing on Production Smoothening in a Utility Sector: A Panel Data Approach
affiliations: , Vivekananda Institute of Professional Studies- Technical Campus, BITS Pilani and University of Delhi

detail.title: Measuring the Impact of Inventory and Marketing on Production Smoothening in a Utility Sector: A Panel Data Approach
detail.abstract: Utility sector is the foundation of economic growth that ensures energy security and industrial productivity along with influencing the living standards especially for the developing countries. The present study critically examines the progressing landscape of India's utility sector, focusing on demand side drifts, executive challenges, financial performances and technological improvements. The study uses extensive panel data of 26 major firms of the utility sector listed in Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) sectoral indices over the period of 10 years (2013-2023). The panel data analysis includes multiple linear regression modelling, random effect analysis and fixed effect regression models capture the heterogeneity in the data. The regression model indicates that change in cost of goods sold (proxy variable of demand), marketing expenses, profit before interest and tax (PBIT) and inventories are significantly impacting the change in cost of production (proxy variable for production). Between ordinary least square (OLS) and random effect, Breusch pagan test concluded that random effect is better approach which shows time invariability. After that Hausman test confirms that there is temporal dynamism present in data and hence the fixed effect prevails. The study provides valuable insights for optimizing production smoothening and hence the operational efficiency based on financial performance.

title: From Parthenon to PMBOK: A Comparative Analysis of Public Works Management
affiliations: Department of Business Administration, University of Thessaly, Larissa, Greece and University of Thessaly

detail.title: From Parthenon to PMBOK: A Comparative Analysis of Public Works Management
detail.abstract: This article examines the management of public works in Ancient Greece in comparison with modern project management methodologies, with the aim of investigating whether basic principles of modern project management were present in ancient practices. Through qualitative and comparative analysis of emblematic public works, such as the Parthenon and the Tunnel of Eupalinos, organizational structures, governance mechanisms, cost control practices, quality requirements and accountability systems are explored in their historical and institutional context. Modern international project management standards (PMBOK, PRINCE2 and ISO 21500) are leveraged as conceptual reference frameworks rather than normative models, allowing for the identification of analogies without outdated interpretations. The findings show that public works in Ancient Greece were implemented within structured institutional systems, with distinct phases, public financial oversight, collective decision-making, and strong social and political accountability. The study highlights the timelessness of basic principles of project management and offers theoretical and critical reflections on the modern practice of public works.

title: Constructing Development Miracles: A Theory of National Transformational Capacity and the Middle-Income Trap

detail.title: Constructing Development Miracles: A Theory of National Transformational Capacity and the Middle-Income Trap
detail.abstract: While most developing countries reach middle-income levels, many become trapped in long periods of stagnation, with only a few achieving sustained development breakthroughs. This article proposes the Theory of Constructing Development Miracles, which reframes development as a purposeful national transformation shaped by governance choices, rather than a spontaneous outcome of market-driven growth. The theory identifies three mutually reinforcing transformations: (i) institutional change toward a developmental state capable of strategic coordination; (ii) economic restructuring from growth by expansion toward upgradingbased development; and (iii) the transformation of national capabilities from passive absorption to endogenous learning and innovation. Development miracles materialize when these transformations are aligned, generating cumulative and self-reinforcing dynamics that push national development trajectories beyond critical thresholds.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces and formalizes a previously unarticulated regime in human technological development: the coupled operation of Adoption-Driven Authority Transfer (ADAT), Closed-Loop Self-Improvement Intervals (CLSI), Recursive Leverage Factor (RLF), and a globally networked node ecosystem. While each component has partial analogues in existing scientific, economic, or engineering literature, their integration produces a qualitatively distinct phenomenon in which authority migrates from humans to technical systems as a structural consequence of scale, speed, and competitive coordination. The resulting regime explains why non-adoption becomes punitive, governance lags become irreversible, and legitimacy diverges from control prior to artificial superintelligence. This work establishes the novelty of the combined framework and provides a minimal mathematical formulation capturing its authority-generating dynamics.

title: The Business Tsunami Mindset
affiliations: Tilburg University and INSEAD

detail.title: The Business Tsunami Mindset
detail.abstract: A business tsunami is a major disruptive event that seems to hit a business out of nowhere with disastrous effects, although in retrospect one will find that it has been quietly building up pressure and strength in some peripheral part of the business for considerable time. How well a company responds to such a business tsunami depends on quite a number of things: (1) how early it makes sense of the impending disaster, (2) how quickly it decides upon an appropriate course of action, (3) how well and quickly it manages to implement these decisions and (4) how well it learns from previous tsunami and how it dealt with them. This paper analyses business tsunami and the need to accelerate the management decision cycle to respond to them. It uses ASML as a case study.

detail.abstract: This note introduces two related concepts-Closed-Loop Self-Improvement Interval (CLSI) and Recursive Leverage Factor (RLF)-intended to describe and analyze the dynamics of recursive improvement in advanced artificial intelligence systems. Existing terminology in AI, economics, and systems theory insufficiently captures the interaction between iteration speed and per-iteration impact in self-improving systems. CLSI and RLF are proposed to fill this gap by separating time per improvement loop from effect per loop, providing clearer analytical leverage for understanding runaway dynamics, governance challenges, and loss of human control.

title: Unit Economics-Driven Profitability Assessment of Quick-Commerce Expansion into Tier-2 Indian Cities

detail.title: Unit Economics-Driven Profitability Assessment of Quick-Commerce Expansion into Tier-2 Indian Cities

detail.abstract:
India's quick-commerce industry has expanded rapidly as consumers adopt faster grocery delivery, but profitability remains unsettled. While Tier-1 cities have driven most of the sector's growth so far, they are also characterized by intense competition, high marketing intensity, and operational complexity. This has led many platforms to consider Tier-2 cities as a potential path to stronger unit economics.
This paper evaluates whether Tier-2 expansion meaningfully improves financial outcomes at the unit level. Using a unit economics lens, it compares revenue drivers, cost structures, contribution margins, and breakeven behaviour across Tier-1 and Tier-2 markets. The analysis finds that although Tier-2 cities benefit from structurally lower operating costs and lower acquisition spend, these advantages are partly offset by lower basket sizes, weaker monetisation maturity, and less stable demand density.
Overall, Tier-2 expansion improves economics only under specific operating conditions—particularly where demand is sufficiently concentrated, delivery costs remain controlled, and customer engagement matures beyond occasional use. The paper concludes by presenting a decision framework to help firms determine when Tier-2 expansion strengthens economics, and when it risks widening cash burn.

title: Explainable Hyper-Heuristics for Sustainable Decision Support: A Transparent Learning Framework with Valid Inequalities
affiliations: , ,  and Lebanese University

detail.title: Explainable Hyper-Heuristics for Sustainable Decision Support: A Transparent Learning Framework with Valid Inequalities
detail.abstract: This study proposes an Explainable Hyper-Heuristic (X-HH) framework for sustainable decision support, integrating learning-based heuristic selection with interpretability and mathematical rigor. The framework combines a pool of low-level heuristics, adaptive selection via contextual learning, acceptance and termination criteria, and an explainable AI (XAI) layer to enhance transparency. A formal multi-objective mathematical formulation is introduced to model cost, emissions, and equity trade-offs, and valid inequalities are proposed to strengthen the formulation and guide heuristic search. Two case studies—sustainable manufacturing scheduling and green vehicle routing demonstrate the method’s effectiveness. Across 300 generated instances, X-HH achieves 10–15\% improvement in hypervolume and 20–30\% reduction in equity dispersion over baseline heuristics, while providing interpretable selection rationales. This framework establishes a bridge between adaptive metaheuristics, mathematical optimization, and responsible AI for sustainable operations.

title: FIRST LOOK - Human Capacity at the Boundary of Flight: Preparing the Conceptual Ground for Advanced Human Performance Systems

detail.title: FIRST LOOK - Human Capacity at the Boundary of Flight: Preparing the Conceptual Ground for Advanced Human Performance Systems
detail.abstract: For centuries, human flight has functioned as a revealing boundary condition for human capability. Early failures of human-powered flight demonstrated that biological structures-muscle mass, skeletal configuration, metabolic output, and sensorimotor coordination-were insufficient to overcome gravitational and aerodynamic constraints. Rather than extinguishing the pursuit of flight, these limitations catalyzed the development of machines designed explicitly to compensate for human incapability. As aviation matured, however, technological solutions introduced new constraints at the cognitive level, shifting the primary source of operational risk from mechanical failure to human factors such as attention, spatial orientation, workload management, and decision-making under uncertainty.

title: Post-Pandemic Assessment of World Heritage Church Operations in the Philippines: Development of a Crisis Management Model
affiliations: University of Santo Tomas, University of Santo Tomas and University of Santo Tomas

detail.title: Post-Pandemic Assessment of World Heritage Church Operations in the Philippines: Development of a Crisis Management Model
detail.abstract: Philippine religious and cultural institutions, particularly the four World Heritage Churches,Miag-ao, Paoay, San Agustin (Intramuros), and Sta. Maria, were also vulnerable to the COVID-19 pandemic. These churches are places of worship and cultural preservation, but their crisis management strategies were rarely explored. This study assessed crisis management implementation during the pandemic, identified challenges and opportunities, and future plans as inputs to propose a model applicable to world heritage churches. Mixed methods design is used. Quantitative data from a parishioner survey measured crisis management implementation throughout four phases of preparation, prevention, incident management, and post-crisis rehabilitation. Structured interviews with parish administrators and officers yielded qualitative data. Thematic analysis studied interview transcripts, while descriptive statistics assessed survey findings. Triangulation enhanced understanding by combining both data types. Quantitative findings showed “Very High” crisis management implementation, while qualitative insights showed structural flaws, overreliance on external players, and unequal parish capacities. Adaptive leadership, community cohesion, digital innovation, and crisis response institutionalization were revealed in the themes. Subsequently, the CROSS-CAREFramework (Church Resilience and Operational Strategies for Sustainability – Community, Adaptation, Recovery, Engagement) was proposed based on findings. The framework promotes crisis resilience via planning, prevention, adaptive response, and recovery by aligning faith, heritage, and commerce. It supports partnerships between church and community with government, and puts in place sustainable, internationally relevant processes and procedures into the heritage church operations.

title: An Adaptable 3D Point Cloud Framework for Multi-Type Weld Segmentation and Dimensional Measurement
affiliations: University of South China, University of South China, University of South China, Xiangtan University and CRRC Zhuzhou Locomotive Co. Ltd

detail.title: An Adaptable 3D Point Cloud Framework for Multi-Type Weld Segmentation and Dimensional Measurement
detail.abstract: Accurate weld quality inspection is critical to the safety and reliability of structural components in aerospace, automotive manufacturing, and construction engineering. At present, 3D point cloud vision based weld inspection methods provide a promising pathway to improve detection accuracy and automation. However, when dealing with multiple weld types, such as flat welds, fillet welds, girth welds, pipe to pipe fillet welds, intersecting welds, spatially curved welds, and tube sheet welds, under complex working conditions, they still suffer from insufficient segmentation robustness, a lack of a unified geometric reference framework, and limited dimensional measurement accuracy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel 3D point cloud based method for weld segmentation and dimensional measurement. A curvature driven dimensionality reduction and morphological topology constrained segmentation algorithm, referred to as CDR MTS, is developed to achieve stable segmentation across multiple weld types. A moving weld seam coordinate system, referred to as MWCS, is established to provide a unified geometric reference for different weld configurations. Based on this framework, weld dimensions including length, width, and height are accurately measured by combining tangent projection accumulation and normal section peak extraction. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves errors within ±0.41 mm for width and height and within ±0.68 mm for length when compared with manual measurements. The results demonstrate high accuracy and stability, providing a general and precise solution for intelligent weld quality inspection and digital manufacturing.

title: Anthropomorphism and Gamification in Building Customer Experience in Digital Products

detail.title: Anthropomorphism and Gamification in Building Customer Experience in Digital Products

detail.abstract: This article examines how anthropomorphism and gamification jointly shape customer experience (CX) in digital products. Drawing on the psychological literature on anthropomorphism—particularly accounts that link humanization to needs for understanding, control, and social connection—it argues that assigning human-like cues (e.g., voice, character, affect) can function as a cognitive and relational shortcut that reduces perceived friction in interactions. The paper then conceptualizes gamification as the application of game-design elements in non-game contexts and reviews core mechanisms such as feedback, progression, rewards, and ritualized return patterns. Using two illustrative cases—Duolingo and InPost—the analysis shows how anthropomorphic “brand protagonists” and game mechanics (e.g., streaks, points, leagues) can reinforce one another to support engagement, interpretability, and habit formation. At the same time, the discussion highlights boundary conditions and ethical risks, including schema incongruence and the potential for manipulative pressure via loss aversion and attention-capturing nudges. The article concludes with a practical, design-oriented checklist for implementing anthropomorphism and gamification responsibly, emphasizing congruence, meaningful mechanics, and safeguards for user well-being.

title: The Dynamics of Less-Idiocy: A Model of Organizational Adaptation under Drift
affiliations: Independent Researcher

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None

detail.abstract: Conventional models treat intelligence as a stock variable proportional to accumulated knowledge, violating thermodynamic constraints on finite agents embedded in irreversible time. We define idiocy as divergence between internal models and a drifting environment, and define intelligence as its negative time derivative. We introduce cognitive stiffness as the energetic cost of reorientation and refine it by identity mass, the degree to which internal commitments are load-bearing for the self. We derive a critical stiffness threshold governing epistemic stability and prove finite-time collapse under unopposed structural accretion. As a corollary, any frozenparameter learner in a drifting environment is mathematically guaranteed to accumulate divergence. We identify a Safety-Collapse Paradox, proving that organizational safeguards which increase structural accretion without proportional pruning mathematically guarantee catastrophic failure under drift. We further derive a pruning budget law for stability, propose kinetic measures of cognition, and introduce the Less-Idiot Index as a domain-invariant predictor of epistemic survival under drift.

title: Spatiotemporal Evolution and Prediction of Coupled Coordination Between Ecological Conservation and High-Quality Development in the Yellow River Basin

detail.title: Spatiotemporal Evolution and Prediction of Coupled Coordination Between Ecological Conservation and High-Quality Development in the Yellow River Basin
detail.abstract: To assess the synergy between ecological protection and high-quality development in the Yellow River Basin and to capture its spatiotemporal dynamics, this study constructs a dual-system evaluation framework. An integrated index system is established and measured using the entropy weight–TOPSIS method combined with a coupling coordination model. Furthermore, spatial autocorrelation analysis, Dagum Gini coefficient decomposition, and the GM (1,1) grey prediction model are introduced to systematically characterize the evolutionary trend and regional heterogeneity of the coordination level. The results reveal that from 2007 to 2023, the coupling coordination degree steadily increased and is projected to reach 0.676 by 2030, presenting an overall trend of “steady improvement with regional differentiation.” The Moran’s I index continues to rise, indicating an enhancement of spatial agglomeration.This study provides empirical evidence for advancing the synergistic optimization of ecological and development systems in the Yellow River Basin and offers a reference pathway for promoting regional collaborative governance in other major river basins.

title: AI-Enhanced Marketing Mix Modeling: Integrating ML, XAI, and LLMs for Greater Accuracy, Interpretability, and Actionability
affiliations: and University of Rochester

detail.title: AI-Enhanced Marketing Mix Modeling: Integrating ML, XAI, and LLMs for Greater Accuracy, Interpretability, and Actionability
detail.abstract: This paper proposes an AI-enhanced Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) framework that integrates machine learning (ML), explainable AI (XAI), and large language models (LLMs) to evaluate marketing effectiveness with improved predictive accuracy, interpretability, and practical applicability. Moving beyond traditional MMM approaches, the framework employs the XGBoost algorithm to capture nonlinear relationships between multichannel marketing investments and business outcomes. SHAP analysis further enhances model interpretability through feature-importance rankings, beeswarm visualizations, and dependence plots that quantify each channel's marginal contribution. In addition, a Claude-based LLM module translates complex model outputs into natural-language performance insights and budget allocation recommendations, lowering technical barriers and improving decisionmaking actionability. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with an OLS baseline, the XGBoost model significantly improves predictive performance, increasing R² from 0.8572 to 0.9123 while reducing RMSE and MAE by 21.7% and 22.8%, respectively. The integrated SHAP and LLM components further elucidate channel impacts and suggest budget optimization strategies, yielding an estimated 18-25% improvement in marketing ROI. Overall, the proposed AI-enhanced MMM framework democratizes advanced marketing analytics by providing businesses with an accessible, automated solution that guides strategic marketing decision-making, enables efficient resource allocation, and improves marketing returns.

title: Working Capital Dynamics and Inflation Cross-Country Evidence from Advanced Economies

detail.title: Working Capital Dynamics and Inflation Cross-Country Evidence from Advanced Economies
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether aggregate changes in corporate working capital help explain inflation dynamics in four major advanced economies. Using quarterly data for the United States, the euro area, the United Kingdom and Japan, the analysis finds a robust relationship only in the United States, where increases in working-capital absorption predict lower inflation after standard controls. Structural-break tests show that this relationship strengthens markedly during the global financial crisis (GFC) and the COVID period, indicating that the working-capital channel is state dependent and becomes more informative when financial and logistical constraints tighten. The absence of similar patterns in the euro area, the United Kingdom and Japan suggests that institutional features, particularly the stability of bank-intermediated credit, buffer firms’ short-term liquidity needs and limit macroeconomic effects. The results show that firm-level liquidity conditions can influence inflation in specific institutional settings and highlight the importance of financial structure in inflation analysis.

title: Research to Improve the Quality, Impact, and Value of Home and Community-Based Services
affiliations: Harvard University, Harvard University, University of Pennsylvania - Perelman School of Medicine and Harvard School of Public Health

detail.title: Research to Improve the Quality, Impact, and Value of Home and Community-Based Services
detail.abstract:
Nearly eight million Americans use Medicaid home and community-based services (HCBS) to support long-term services and supports for people with disabilities. Recent legislative changes to Medicaid will require states to make difficult choices about how best to meet these long-term services and supports needs. This paper first characterizes the unique goals of HCBS, which differ from those of traditional medical care services, and the state-federal financing and administrative structure of HCBS. Next, based on a review of the literature and input from a panel of experts in HCBS policy and research, we summarize existing evidence and knowledge gaps regarding the quality and cost implications of HCBS at the federal, state, and direct service provision levels. Based on gaps in the evidence, we propose a research agenda related to state-federal incentives, state program choices regarding HCBS financing and delivery models, and the settings and supports for direct service provision. Finally, we describe existing and novel data sources and other opportunities that could accelerate research to fill these evidence gaps and support states and others in designing, implementing, and delivering sustainable, high-quality HCBS.

title: Tenure-Dependent Severance Costs and Labor Market Dynamics over the Life Cycle
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill, College of Arts and Sciences, Department of Economics, Students and University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill

detail.title: Tenure-Dependent Severance Costs and Labor Market Dynamics over the Life Cycle
detail.abstract:
We study the labor market effects of tenure-dependent severance pay systems that tie firing costs to workers’ accumulated earnings histories. We develop an overlapping-generations search-and-matching model in which firms face increasing separation costs over the employment relationship. Using administrative employer–employee data from Brazil, we estimate the model and show that tenure-dependent severance costs induce labor hoarding among low-productivity, long-tenured workers who would not be hired if unemployed. These distortions are strongest late in the life cycle, when firms optimally delay separation to avoid severance obligations, while simultaneously imposing higher hiring thresholds on older unemployed workers with shorter continuation values. These forces imply that tenure-based severance policies protect employment histories rather than productivity, shaping labor market dynamics over the life cycle and generating allocative inefficiencies.

title: Kalshi and the Rise of Macro Markets
affiliations: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, Northwestern University and Johns Hopkins University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Kalshi and the Rise of Macro Markets
detail.abstract:
Prediction markets offer a new market-based approach to measuring macroeconomic expectations in real-time. We evaluate the accuracy of prediction market-implied forecasts from Kalshi, the largest federally regulated prediction market overseen by the CFTC. We compare Kalshi with more traditional survey and market-implied forecasts, examine how expectations respond to macroeconomic and financial news, and how policy signals are interpreted by market participants. Our results suggest that Kalshi markets provide a high-frequency, continuously updated, distributionally rich benchmark that is valuable to both researchers and policymakers.

title: Aggregate Productivity with Discrete Choice
affiliations: University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Aggregate Productivity with Discrete Choice
detail.abstract:
This paper quantifies aggregate productivity in general equilibrium economies where agents with heterogeneous preferences make discrete choices between locations and occupations. We show how the conventional tools of welfare economics, like cost-benefit analysis, can be extended to these settings. Following Debreu (1951), we measure the change in aggregate productivity as the maximum reduction in total factor productivity such that it is possible to make every household at least indifferent to their status quo allocation. Aggregate productivity rises if primary factors can be saved while keeping every household at least indifferent. We characterize this measure of efficiency in terms of compensated supply and demand curves. We show that, to a first-order approximation, the elasticity of aggregate productivity to productivity shocks is given by sales shares (regardless of preferences and technologies). We also provide second-order approximations in terms of elasticities of uncompensated supply and demand curves. We contrast our approach with some popular alternative measures of aggregate efficiency and welfare: real GDP, the cross-sectional average of utilities, and the sum of compensating variations, and show that these alternative measures have serious flaws.

title: Deforestation-Driven Disaster Vulnerability: Triangulating Statistical Evidence with Public Sentiment in the November 2025 Sumatra Floods, Indonesia

detail.title: Deforestation-Driven Disaster Vulnerability: Triangulating Statistical Evidence with Public Sentiment in the November 2025 Sumatra Floods, Indonesia

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have influenced this work

detail.abstract: Indonesia experienced catastrophic flooding and landslides in November 2025, claiming over 960 lives across Sumatra. While official narratives often attribute such disasters solely to extreme rainfall, this study investigates the amplifying role of deforestation through a mixed-methods triangulation approach. We analyzed environmental data from 75 administrative units across three Sumatran provinces (Aceh, North Sumatra, West Sumatra) alongside 114,735 social media posts from Twitter/X (47,625) and YouTube comments (67,110). Statistical analysis reveals an indirect evidence chain: deforestation correlates significantly with increased river discharge (ρ = +0.58, p < 0.0001), which in turn correlates with flood severity (ρ = +0.35, p = 0.002). Districts along major rivers experienced 1.6 times greater severity (p = 0.005), while upstream areas suffered 3.0 times worse landslide impacts (p = 0.004). Critically, high-deforestation areas experienced 3.5 times worse flooding despite receiving comparable rainfall, demonstrating that land cover vulnerability, not precipitation intensity, determines disaster outcomes. Spatial autocorrelation confirms significant clustering of deforestation and disaster severity (Moran's I = 0.31, p = 0.0003). Sentiment analysis reveals public discourse transitioning from grief (sadness 31.9%, declining at-1.49%/day) toward accountability-seeking (anger 15.6%, increasing at +0.72%/day). Blame attribution concentrates on government institutions (72.1%), with 25.3% of posts explicitly mentioning environmental drivers. Triangulation yields 80% alignment between online public discourse and statistical evidence, with a critical gap in mechanistic understanding: while communities correctly identify deforestation and governmental responsibility, discourse lacks the hydrological literacy linking forest loss to flooding. These findings support upstream watershed protection, land cover vulnerability integration in early warning systems, and mechanism-focused risk communication.

title: Never Enough: Dynamic Status Incentives in Organizations
affiliations: University of Chicago - Department of Economics, Harvard University and University of Zurich - UBS International Center of Economics in Society

detail.title: Never Enough: Dynamic Status Incentives in Organizations
detail.abstract:
We study the ability of a firm to elicit repeated effort from workers by creating a “rat race” of hierarchical status-based incentives. We examine performance using data on over 5,000 German air force pilots during World War II. Pilots’ effort is hard to monitor; motivation is key to success. Fighter pilot performance increases markedly as they approach eligibility for a medal before falling off upon receipt of the award. The same effort path repeats itself as the pilot nears the next higher-prestige medal. Status-conscious pilots also exert more effort when new medals are introduced. We show that medals serve as substitutes for other forms of status. Medal cachet declines over time as lower-ability pilots receive them, making the introduction of new medals desirable. These results suggest that a tiered, expanding system of status-based incentives can repeatedly leverage worker status concerns to extract effort.

title: Marginal Admission to Elite High Schools: Long-run Effects on Labor Market Outcomes
affiliations: Centro de Investigación y Docencia Económicas (CIDE), , Banco de Mexico and University of Tennessee, Knoxville - College of Business Administration - Department of Economics

detail.title: Marginal Admission to Elite High Schools: Long-run Effects on Labor Market Outcomes
detail.abstract:
We estimate the long-run effects of marginal admission to elite public high schools on students' labor supply in the context of Mexico City's centralized high school admission system. Using a regression discontinuity approach, we compare students whose placement exam scores are just above and just below the elite admission threshold. We find that five and ten years after the admission exam, marginally admitted students are less likely to be employed in the formal private sector, and, if employed, they earn lower wages. However, these employment and wage gaps close after 15 years. Moreover, we find that marginal admission to elite high schools leads to delayed entry into the formal labor market, and, at least in the short run, students in elite high schools seem to sort into lower-productivity firms and industries.

title: Pricing Residential Mortgage Credit Risk in the Post-GFC Era
affiliations: , Columbia University Graduate School of Business and Columbia University

detail.title: Pricing Residential Mortgage Credit Risk in the Post-GFC Era
detail.abstract:
Following the Great Financial Crisis (GFC), the Credit Risk Transfer (CRT) bond market emerged as a new asset class in U.S. mortgage market. We develop an asset pricing framework for CRTs consistent with Treasury, corporate bond, and housing markets. Our analysis reveals that the Government-Sponsored Enterprises compensate investors approximately fairly on average, though they overpay for low-risk tranches and underpay for high-risk ones. Additionally, the post-GFC guarantee fee increases broadly align with underlying credit risk. We find significant reverse cross-subsidization, where high-credit-risk borrowers subsidize low-risk ones. The 2023 reform partially corrected this cross-subsidization.

title: How Adaptable Are American Workers to AI-Induced Job Displacement?
affiliations: Centre for the Governance of AI and Centre for the Governance of AI

detail.title: How Adaptable Are American Workers to AI-Induced Job Displacement?
detail.abstract:
We construct an occupation-level adaptive capacity index that measures a set of worker characteristics relevant for navigating job transitions if displaced, covering 356 occupations that represent 95.9% of the U.S. workforce. We find that AI exposure and adaptive capacity are positively correlated: many occupations highly exposed to AI contain workers with relatively strong means to manage a job transition. Of the 37.1 million workers in the top quartile of AI exposure, 26.5 million are in occupations that also have above-median adaptive capacity, leaving them comparatively well-equipped to handle job transitions if displacement occurs. At the same time, 6.1 million workers (4.2% of the workforce in our sample) work in occupations that are both highly exposed and where workers have low expected adaptive capacity. These workers are concentrated in clerical and administrative roles. Importantly, AI exposure reflects potential changes to work tasks, not inevitable displacement; only some of the changes brought on by AI will result in job loss. By distinguishing between highly exposed workers with relatively strong means to adjust and those with limited adaptive capacity, our analysis shows that exposure measures alone can obscure both areas of resilience to technological change and concentrated pockets of elevated vulnerability if displacement were to occur.

title: Business Concentration around the World: 1900-2020

detail.title: Business Concentration around the World: 1900-2020
detail.abstract:
We collect new data to document the long-run evolution of the firm size distribution in ten market-based economies in Asia, Europe, North America, and Oceania, where we can obtain comprehensive coverage of the population of firms. Around the world, we observe prevalent increases in the concentration of sales, net income, and equity capital over the past century. These trends hold in the aggregate and at the industry level. Meanwhile, employment concentration has been stable over the long run in most cases. The evidence shows that the rising dominance of large firms is a pervasive phenomenon, not limited to the recent decades or the United States, and that large firms often achieve greater scale without proportionally more workers.

title: AI in Charge: Large-Scale Experimental Evidence on Electric Vehicle Charging Demand
affiliations: Columbia University, Centre for Net Zero, University College London and Centre for Net Zero

detail.title: AI in Charge: Large-Scale Experimental Evidence on Electric Vehicle Charging Demand
detail.abstract:
One of the promising opportunities offered by AI to support the decarbonization of electricity grids is to align demand with low-carbon supply. We evaluated the effects of one of the world’s largest AI managed EV charging tariffs (a retail electricity pricing plan) using a large-scale natural field experiment. The tariff dynamically controlled vehicle charging to follow real-time wholesale electricity prices and coordinate and optimize charging for the grid and the consumer through AI. We randomized financial incentives to encourage enrollment onto the tariff. Over more than a year, we found that the tariff led to a 42% reduction in household electricity demand during peak hours, with 100% of this demand shifted to lower-cost and lower-carbon-intensity periods. The tariff generated substantial consumer savings, while demonstrating potential to lower producer costs, energy system costs, and carbon emissions through significant load shifting. Overrides of the AI algorithm were low, suggesting that this tariff was likely more efficient than a real-time-pricing tariff without AI, given our theoretical framework. We found similar plug-in and override behavior in several markets, including the UK, US, Germany, and Spain, implying the potential for comparable demand and welfare effects. Our findings highlight the potential for scalable AI managed charging and its substantial welfare gains for the electricity system and society. We also show that experimental estimates differed meaningfully from those obtained via non-randomized difference-in-differences analysis, due to differences in the samples in the two evaluation strategies, although we can reconcile the estimates with observables.

title: Teaching Economics to the Machines

detail.title: Teaching Economics to the Machines
detail.abstract:
Structural economic models, while parsimonious and interpretable, often exhibit poor data fit and limited forecasting performance. Machine learning models, by contrast, offer substantial flexibility but are prone to overfitting and weak out-of-distribution generalization. We propose a theory-guided transfer learning framework that integrates structural restrictions from economic theory into machine learning models. The approach pre-trains a neural network on synthetic data generated by a structural model and then fine-tunes it using empirical data, allowing potentially misspecified economic restrictions to inform and regularize learning on empirical data. Applied to option pricing, our model substantially outperforms both structural and purely data-driven benchmarks, with especially large gains in small samples, under unstable market conditions, and when model misspecification is limited. Beyond performance, the framework provides diagnostics for improving structural models and introduces a new model-comparison metric based on data-model complementarity.

detail.abstract:
We measure how frontier research frames what is normatively at stake along the efficiency and equity dimension. We develop and validate an LLM-based measurement pipeline and apply it to 27,464 full-text journal articles from 1950 to 2021. Efficiency focused framing rises through the late 1980s, then declines as equity related framing expands after 1990, especially in applied work and policy evaluations. By 2021, papers with an equity component are about as common as papers framed purely around efficiency. President transmittal letters in the Economic Report of the President show a similar post 1990 shift toward equity, providing an external benchmark.

title: A Model of Artificial Jagged Intelligence
affiliations: University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: A Model of Artificial Jagged Intelligence
detail.abstract:
Generative AI systems often display highly uneven performance across tasks that appear “nearby”: they can be excellent on one prompt and confidently wrong on another with only small changes in wording or context. We call this phenomenon Artificial Jagged Intelligence (AJI). This paper develops a tractable economic model of AJI that treats adoption as an information problem: users care about local reliability, but typically observe only coarse, global quality signals. In a baseline one-dimensional landscape, truth is a rough Brownian process, and the model “knows” scattered points drawn from a Poisson process. The model interpolates optimally, and the local error is measured by posterior variance. We derive an adoption threshold for a blind user, show that experienced errors are amplified by the inspection paradox, and interpret scaling laws as denser coverage that improves average quality without eliminating jaggedness. We then study mastery and calibration: a calibrated user who can condition on local uncertainty enjoys positive expected value even in domains that fail the blind adoption test. Modelling mastery as learning a reliability map via Gaussian process regression yields a learning-rate bound driven by information gain, clarifying when discovering “where the model works” is slow. Finally, we study how scaling interacts with discoverability: when calibrated signals and user mastery accelerate the harvesting of scale improvements, and when opacity can make gains from scaling effectively invisible.

title: Sociality in Tribes

detail.title: Sociality in Tribes
detail.abstract:
This work presents a unified formal framework—the Tribal Grammar System (TGS)—for analyzing the structural dynamics of human social organization across evolutionary, religious, cultural, and commercial domains. The framework posits that all social entities can be rigorously described by a triple consisting of an Ideology of Satisfaction, a Fantasy of unfulfilled desire, and a Manifesto of behavioral rules.

Building on this grammar, the Genetic Tribal Model (GTM) is introduced as an evolutionary hypothesis, proposing that specific "Unit Axioms"—including the Chieftain, the Warrior, and a specialized non-reproductive Alpha Class—emerged as adaptive solutions to intra-tribal conflict in early hominids. This model reinterprets eusociality in humans as a function of these specialized castes.

A central contribution of the work is Mathematical Theology, which applies the TGS to formalize religious doctrines as structural configurations. The work provides axiomatic derivations of the Nicene Creed (as a stable "Trilithon" structure) , the Shema of Judaism, and the Shahada of Islam. It further applies this calculus to analyze historical schisms, offering formal reconciliation paths for the Filioque controversy in Christianity and the Sunni-Shia schism in Islam through parameter alignment.

The work extends this formalism to the Social Computability Thesis, arguing that the Tribal Grammar System constitutes a Turing-complete language for social description, implying that social dynamics are computational processes subject to undecidability. This theoretical insight informs a novel approach to Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) alignment, proposing a "G6" (Pharaonic) architecture based on theological topology rather than ethics to ensure stability over civilizational timescales.

Finally, the text outlines the practical application of these theories through the design of Leviathans—large-scale commercial infrastructure ventures (AFR Healthcare, AFR Energy, AFR Transportation). These entities are structured as "Divine Houses" or "Pyramids" designed to channel social energy into permanent value creation, regulated by a rigorous ethical framework prohibiting discrimination. Sociality in Tribes thus attempts a complete synthesis of the biological roots, theological expressions, and future technological architectures of human cooperation.

title: Risk Management as the Key Mediator in Retail Margin Trading Performance

detail.title: Risk Management as the Key Mediator in Retail Margin Trading Performance
detail.abstract: The facilities offered to traders who have access to the Indian stock market on a retail basis have grown phenomenally in recent times. One such facility is the Margin Trading. The effect on the stock market traders' performances due to the increased use of Margin Trading is not fully understood. The present research focuses on the Margin Trading Function. The research attempts to appreciate the correlation between the risks which traders have to undergo with retail trader's financial outcomes. The research is of a quantitative basis. The research targets 246 retail traders in India and uses an SEM framework to understand the data imputed. The results demonstrate an important conclusion: The Function of Margin Trading is not applicable to financial outcomes directly. The only way it can be correlated is because of risk control. The results indicate that MTF use does not have a direct impact on financial risk outcomes but rather compels traders to strengthen their risk control processes. It is this increased risk control which leads to the financial outcomes. The research attempts to redefine the control which they have on their leverage. It is suggested that the control does not only increase the risk but the order discipline which accompanies it should also be appreciated.

title: The Constitutional Future Of Trademark Tarnishment
affiliations: Florida State University - College of Law

detail.title: The Constitutional Future Of Trademark Tarnishment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no personal or financial relationship with people or organizations that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this research.

detail.abstract:
Forthcoming William & Mary Bill of Rights Journal (2026)

This article is the first to examine whether trademark anti-tarnishment laws should be deemed constitutional after the Supreme Court's 2024 decision in Vidal v. Elster. Anti-tarnishment laws protect famous brands from uses that could damage their reputation, even when consumers are not confused about who makes the tarnishing product.

The Supreme Court recently declared some trademark registration restrictions unconstitutional in Matal v. Tam and Iancu v. Brunetti. In these cases, the Court struct down federal laws that prevented registration of "disparaging" and "scandalous or immoral" trademarks. The Court held the registration bars were unconstitutional viewpoint-based restrictions. Many legal scholars argue that following Tam and Brunetti, anti-tarnishment laws are also unconstitutional viewpoint-based restrictions because they allow trademark owners to silence criticism and negative commentary.

However, Elster provides new frameworks for evaluating anti-tarnishment laws. In Elster, an applicant was barred from registering a mark critical of Donald Trump and challenged the bar as an unconstitutional speech restriction. The Justices agreed that the provision, which barred registration of a mark that "consists of or comprises a name, portrait, or signature identifying a particular living individual except by his written consent," was a content-based but viewpoint-neutral restriction. But the Court did not apply strict scrutiny to the provision, even though content-based laws often trigger strict scrutiny. The majority instead utilized a more flexible approach, examining the historical tradition of similar trademark restrictions and their co-existence with the First Amendment. Four concurring Justices would instead have held the restriction reasonably serves trademark law's fundamental purposes of preventing consumer confusion and protecting mark-owner goodwill.

This article argues that anti-tarnishment protection should survive constitutional challenges under either approach. These laws target harm from incongruous associations - including using a luxury brand on inferior products - rather than suppressing particular viewpoints. They safeguard the commercial goodwill that trademark owners have developed through years of business investment, and that goodwill provides valuable sorting signals to consumers. This article further cautions against using constitutional scrutiny to dismantle reasonable commercial regulations, including trademark laws generally and the anti-tarnishment provision in particular.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces and formalizes the Adoption-Driven Authority Transfer (ADAT) model, a structural account of how human decision authority migrates to technical systems as a consequence of ordinary adoption dynamics. The model explains loss of effective human control without assuming intent, misalignment, or superintelligence. Extending diffusion-of-innovation, path-dependence, and infrastructure-entrenchment theories, ADAT treats authority-not efficiency or output-as the primary endogenous variable. We show how competitive adoption, workflow integration, speed asymmetry, and institutional incentives produce dependency prior to legitimacy, resulting in symbolic oversight, practical irreversibility, and governance lag. The paper provides a rigorous mathematical formalization, identifies falsifiable conditions, and demonstrates the mechanism through a single-vehicle historical analog (GPS navigation). The contribution is a general, durable model applicable across domains, with specific implications for AI governance.

title: Adoption-Driven Authority Transfer: A Structural Model of AI-Human Control

detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel structural model explaining how societies lose effective human control over advanced technological systems-particularly artificial intelligence (AI)-prior to explicit delegation, legitimacy, or governance. Extending classical diffusion-of-innovation, path-dependence, and infrastructureentrenchment frameworks, the model identifies decision authority as an endogenous state variable that degrades as adoption-driven dependency forms. The model predicts a critical threshold at which human oversight becomes symbolic rather than causal and where rollback becomes structurally infeasible despite technical reversibility. Unlike existing AI safety or economic incentive models, this framework does not assume superintelligence, malign intent, or centralized control. Instead, it explains loss of human agency as an emergent, path-dependent outcome of competitive adoption. The paper argues that authority transfer precedes legitimacy resolution and that governance efforts initiated post-dependency are inherently reactive. This constitutes a new model of adoption-driven authority transfer with implications for AI governance, economics, and institutional design.

title: Carefully Tailored: Doctrinal Methods and Empirical Contributions

detail.title: Carefully Tailored: Doctrinal Methods and Empirical Contributions
detail.abstract: Doctrinal research is the distinct methodological approach of lawyers and a core contribution of legal studies to human knowledge. Yet, lawyers do not often explain their doctrinal research methods and by implication struggle to articulate where empirical research can make helpful contributions. The articles suggests that doctrinal research is characterised by three core features that make specific assumptions about law: (1) legal sources are the exclusive avenue for altering rules and principles of law; (2) legal sources are intelligible, coherent, and consistent; and (3) the success of any doctrinal account is contingent on legal sources alone. On this basis, we can appreciate that empirical contributions are essential (1) to an accurate understanding of the law, (2) to critiques, because the law lacks frameworks to evaluate its own operation, and (3) to surveying legal sources. However, this insight comes with a word of caution: not all empirical methods are well suited to providing doctrinally relevant insights and there are some sophisticated pitfalls to avoid along the way.

title: Meta-Analysis of the Effectiveness of Futures Contracts in Hedging Stock Index Risk

detail.abstract: Purpose-Empirical research on the hedge effectiveness with futures contracts has yielded contradictory results, particularly in comparing emerging markets with developed countries. Furthermore, these studies often lack generalizability due to limitations related to time, sample, and methodology. The purpose of this meta-analysis is to explore the significance of this heterogeneity and to document their underlying causes. This endeavor aims to enhance the hedge effectiveness in the futures market and improve the accuracy of empirical research. Design/methodology/approach-In the seven-step approach of this unbiased meta-analysis, we quantitatively analyzed 30 empirical studies employing the random effects model. This analysis encompassed 1,373 empirical tests of the stock index hedge effectiveness by futures contracts, supported by a total of 1,052,225 evaluation samples. Findings-The results indicate that, overall, the hedge effectiveness is significantly positive and heterogeneous. This finding was subjected to testing across 54 sub-samples, which confirmed its robustness. Originality/value-The innovation of this study lies in the meta-analytical identification of the reasons for the observed heterogeneity. Key factors include the duration of the evaluation period, the duration of the estimation period, the evaluation window strategy, the type of underlying asset, hedge strategy, the level of country development, the estimation strategy, and the estimation technique. Understanding these factors significantly enhances the accuracy of empirical research in risk hedging by futures while also improving the effectiveness of participants engaged in risk hedging.

title: Restoring and Strengthening the Ethical Culture at Cornerstone Creation Care Ministries (CCCM)
affiliations: Regent University and VIZJA UNIVERSITY

detail.title: Restoring and Strengthening the Ethical Culture at Cornerstone Creation Care Ministries (CCCM)
detail.abstract:
Cornerstone Creation Care Ministries (CCCM), a Christian animal-welfare nonprofit in Minnesota, faced a grave ethical scandal in 2023–2024 when its founder diverted about $ 250,000 in donor-restricted funds for personal use (Minnesota Attorney General's Office, 2024). The Minnesota Attorney General's settlement required full restitution, removal of leadership, and extensive governance reforms (Minnesota Attorney General's Office, 2024). This report offers a practical, evidence-based plan for the new Chief Executive Officer to rebuild an ethical organizational culture that is legally compliant, biblically rooted, and reputation-protected.

Five key areas are addressed:

Formal and informal cultures: CCCM' s previous misalignment between weak policies and a “founder- can- do- no- wrong” informal norm enabled misconduct. Recommendations include a complete policy overhaul, duty segregation, and intentional interventions (ethics champions, quarterly ethics moments, revised performance metrics) to align both levels.

Ethics and legal compliance: A seven- element compliance program, based on the Federal Sentencing Guidelines and the Evangelical Council for Financial Accountability (ECFA) standards, is outlined. It includes new codes of ethics/conduct, mandatory yearly training, a third- party whistleblower hotline, and technology safeguards.

Biblical framework integration: A six- principle theology of stewardship, integrity, accountability, justice, humility, and love supports all training. A detailed 6- hour biblical ethics curriculum, weekly devotionals, and leadership modeling will embed Scripture into everyday life.

Managing ethical conduct: Tone-at-the-top commitments, psychological safety initiatives, layered monitoring (daily controls, quarterly audits, yearly reviews), and a straightforward discipline matrix will promote and enforce ethical behavior.

Reputation rebuilding: A five-step plan —full public acknowledgment, visible corrective actions, radical transparency, proactive re-engagement, and redemptive storytelling—aims to regain trust. Measurable milestones aim for a 25% donor return by 2026 and for complete recovery by 2029.

title: Liquidity-Driven Breakout Reliability: Why Price Moves Where Liquidity Is Missing
affiliations: and

detail.title: Liquidity-Driven Breakout Reliability: Why Price Moves Where Liquidity Is Missing
detail.abstract: It is widely known that booms are justified with momentum, volatility increase or information storylines. But if the reality of market action is a guide, these justifications are contradicted time and again: visually impressive breakouts don't work, quiet looking moves travel far and long. This paper contends that liquidity structure is the omitted variable. We recast breakouts not as price events, but rather as shifts between high-friction (liquidity-dense) and low-friction (liquidity-sparse) portions of the market. To do so we investigate the use of volume at price analysis, Value Area structures and survival based statistical analysis to analyse over 15,000 breakout events in equity index futures, FX and commodities markets during the period from 2022-2024. We demonstrate that breakouts entering low-volume environments experience significantly increased persistence, accelerated price discovery, and longer continuation lengths relative to breakouts testing high-order volumes. A Kaplan-Meier survival model shows that low-volume-node breakouts have a >70% chance of continuation, high-volume nodes as approximately random. Detailed case studies illustrate the mechanism in practice. Case Studies are provided to show works in application. The findings imply that it is intolerance, rather than aggressiveness, of the order flow which moves prices. This liquidity-focused perspective has implications for market microstructure theory, empirical asset pricing, and applied trading and risk systems.

title: Quantile Hedging in a Self-Exciting Jump Diffusion Model
affiliations: Sorbonne University - Laboratoire de Probabilités, Statistique et Modélisation (LPSM), Université Paris Saclay and University of Pisa - Department of Economics and Management

detail.title: Quantile Hedging in a Self-Exciting Jump Diffusion Model
detail.abstract: In this paper, we consider a version of the stochastic target problem with controlled probability, introduced in [11] and generalized to jump diffusion models in [34], where the state variable's dynamics is driven by a marked point process with stochastic intensity. First, a class of stochastic target problems will be identified where the value function is monotonic in its space variables. The deeper analysis does not pretend to be generic and will subsequently focus on the financial application to the Quantile hedging problem of an European option first introduced in [22]. In particular, we prove the continuity of the quantile hedging price in its space variable by exploiting the natural extension to incomplete markets of its representation as the infimum of a set of superhedging prices. Furthermore, a comparison principle for the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman PDE arising in the context of the quantile hedging problem is proved by extending the results of [12] previously obtained in a Brownian framework.

title: Tourism and Local Livelihoods in Uzbekistan: Income and Stability of Small Vendors Around Historical Sites How Does Tourism Around Uzbekistan's Historical Sites Affect the Income and Stability of Local Small Vendors?

detail.title: Tourism and Local Livelihoods in Uzbekistan: Income and Stability of Small Vendors Around Historical Sites How Does Tourism Around Uzbekistan's Historical Sites Affect the Income and Stability of Local Small Vendors?
detail.abstract: Tourism in Uzbekistan has expanded rapidly in recent years, with foreign arrivals rising from about 5.3 million in 2018 to over 8 million in 2024[1][2]. Much of this growth is concentrated in the UNESCO World Heritage Silk Road cities (Samarkand, Bukhara, Khiva, Shakhrisabz), which attract cultural tourists. This influx has created new income opportunities for local small-scale vendors (souvenir sellers, artisans, food stall operators, local guides), but also introduces significant volatility and inequality. Drawing on government statistics, multilateral reports, field surveys, and media accounts, this paper examines how tourism around Uzbekistan's historical sites affects the livelihoods and economic stability of such vendors. We find that tourism raises incomes and employment for many artisans and service providers, but these gains are often seasonal and informal. Economic mechanisms such as cyclical demand spikes, price competition, and dependency risks cause incomes to fluctuate. Social factors like government incentives for tourism development, infrastructure improvements, and heritage preservation influence market access for vendors. Formal businesses (licensed shops, official guides) tend to capture larger shares of tourism revenue, while many street vendors remain in the informal economy, lacking social protections. The COVID-19 pandemic and other shocks (political reforms, global travel trends) demonstrated vendors’ vulnerability: tourist shutdowns led to sharp income losses.  Moreover, the commercialization of heritage sites can undermine the authenticity of local crafts and raise entry costs for traditional vendors. We conclude that while tourism can boost local incomes, it also fosters structural inequalities and instability for small vendors. Sustainable policies are needed to diversify incomes, support vendor formalization, and preserve community-based cultural practices. Future research and policy should focus on social safety nets, training programs, and inclusive heritage planning to enhance local resilience.
